title: The neck four ways: one mesh per object, instanced, batched, merged
question: For GuitarAlchemist's fretboard, how much do draw calls, CPU time and GPU time change between GaFretboard (one mesh per object, lesson 13), Fretboard3D (InstancedMesh, lesson 13), a BatchedMesh and a merged static geometry, for 1 neck and for 16 necks?
hypothesis: Draw calls drive the CPU time of a frame; the GPU time barely moves, because every strategy draws about the same triangles on an RTX 5080.

predictions.metric: drawCalls, 1 neck with the C major chord (WebGPU)
predictions.predicted: ga 72, instanced 7, batched 4 or fewer, merged 4 or fewer

predictions.metric: median CPU ms per frame, 1 neck, same 1280x720 buffer at pixel ratio 1
predictions.predicted: ga at least 3x the merged neck; all four under 2 ms

predictions.metric: median CPU ms per frame, 16 necks
predictions.predicted: ga at least 10 ms; batched and merged under 1.5 ms

predictions.metric: median GPU ms per frame (timestamp-query), 16 necks
predictions.predicted: the four within 30% of each other

predictions.metric: GA's own pixel ratio (3 at a device pixel ratio of 1) against 1, 1 neck
